newsitem.title: UK: Kerr to head UK diplomatic service.
newsitem.headline: Kerr to head UK diplomatic service.

text.p: Sir John Kerr, currently ambassador in Washington, will take over as head of Britain's diplomatic service in November, the Foreign Office said.
Kerr, who will also become the Foreign Office's top civil servant, will succeed Sir John Cole, who is retiring.
Kerr was Britain's permanent representative in Brussels from 1990 to 1995 and helped to negotiate the Maastricht Treaty on European Union.

With a general election just weeks away, Foreign Secretary Malcom Rifkind informed Labour's foreign affairs spokesman, Robin Cook, last week of Kerr's appointment. Officials said Cook had welcomed it.
Kerr, 54, is expected to leave Washington in the summer.
